title: Marigold's Missing Hat
markdown:
Marigold the macaw had sunset feathers and a voice like a tiny silver bell. She lived in a comfy nook of the Great Jungle with Porridge the possum, grey as morning mist, and Dune the dingo, whose bark was a happy chuckle. Their home was vines and moss, mango-sweet, flower-faint.

The Grand Jungle Talent Show was that very day. The air buzzed like pleased bees. Marigold had a hat she had spent happy hours making: bright green leaves, red berries like tiny jewels, and one feather that held all the colours of rain just after. It was, she would have argued in a court of birds, the most beautiful hat in the jungle.

“One moment,” she chirped. “I must put on my lucky hat. The show would notice if I didn’t.”

The sturdy branch where it had rested in morning sun was empty. Vanished. Her heart went flutter-thump. “Oh, dear.” Bright eyes wide. A perch should not be able to lose a hat.

A single bright feather lay below, winking. Then another. Then another. A trail of sparkling colours, fallen jewels, leading from the cozy nook into dappled shade on the floor.

Dune’s tail drummed the moss. “A feather trail. It must lead to the hat.” He loved a chase, especially one that called itself a quest.

Marigold peered, and a little shiver tickled her tummy. “It leads away from our tree. Into the big jungle.” Beyond her familiar perch the world felt oversized. Leaves rustled like whispers that had not introduced themselves. Shadows stretched as if they had rehearsed.

Porridge, usually content to rustle for juicy grubs, nudged her with his soft grey nose. “We’ll go together. I can look carefully. My eyes like the ground.” His timid look borrowed some determination and did not give it back.

Dune longed to bound. He saw the droop of her crest instead. “We’ll follow. Carefully. No one left behind.”

Off they went, a determined trio, leaving the mango-sweet nook for floor that did not know their names. The trail passed a babbling brook that sang over smooth grey stones and made a fuss about being crossed. Marigold’s knees went jelly. A dragonfly inspected her as if she were late. Porridge showed the flattest stones, a path that asked only for attention and dry claws. “This one. Not that shiny liar.” Dune waited on the far side, tail a bobbing beacon. “You can do it.” Mid-brook she wobbled; Porridge’s tail was suddenly a railing. Each step put a little more ground under the idea of going on.

The trail wound next through whispery ferns, tall and green, tickling noses, a dim green room with too many curtains. Rustle. Marigold wanted her wing for a roof. Something small and uninterested in hats hurried away. Porridge spotted a bright feather caught on a glossy leaf, then a berry from the hat’s brim, still jewel-red. “Look. She came this way, or the wind did, and the wind is a sloppy tailor.” The feather winked them forward. The ferns, once they had a direction, sounded friendlier, like a corridor that had decided to be a hall.

Dune’s paws itched to outrun weather. He remembered the shiver and the quiet pointing, and he slowed, sniffing so they would not miss a clue. “This way.” He nudged a low branch off Marigold’s crest with his head, as if the jungle had grown a doorman.

The trail ended in a small clearing of warm gold. There, caught on the drooping arms of a leafy bush, sat the magnificent hat. A playful gust had tickled it from the perch; the bush had caught it before the floor could claim a jewel.

Marigold gasped and held it. The flutter-thump had clocked off. She had crossed water and ferns. The hat smelled of sunshine and dewy leaves and a little of adventure, which is a scent you cannot sew on in advance.

They hurried back as the first performers stepped onto the talent-show stage. Chatter. A distant drum. The hat settled as if it had only been stretching its leaves.

That evening Marigold sang until fireflies lost their places. Porridge told a story that sent listeners rolling on the grass. Dune performed a wiggly jig that made the monkeys clap until their palms shone. Marigold, hat bright, did not announce a moral. She took the next step onto the moss when the drum asked, and her friends were already there, which was how the hat had been found in the first place.
